name: MC34063ADR2G
title: 1.5 A step-up, step-down and inverting switching regulator controller
summary: A one-chip DC-DC converter controller: a temperature-compensated 1.25 V reference held to 2 %, a comparator, an oscillator whose duty cycle is gated by a current limit, a driver and a 1.5 A bipolar output switch. With an inductor, a diode, a timing capacitor, a sense resistor and a divider it builds a buck, a boost or an inverting converter from 3.0 V to 40 V in, switching at up to 100 kHz. The MC34063A and SC34063A cover 0 to +70 °C, the MC33063A and SC33063A -40 to +85 °C, the MC33063AV and NCV33063A -40 to +125 °C.
key_figures: up to 100 kHz; 33 kHz typ with CT = 1.0 nF

This cuts the off time at 30 kHz and above, and worsens when hot. The Darlington connection cannot saturate and does not show it. For saturated drive the forced β of the switch, IC(output) / (IC(driver) - 7.0 mA), should be at least 10.
The 7.0 mA in note 6 is the current the 100 Ω resistor in the driver's emitter takes before the output switch starts to conduct.

circuits.title: Step-up converter
circuits.description: Boosts 12 V to 28 V at 175 mA. The output switch pulls the bottom of the 170 µH inductor to ground; when it opens the inductor's current flows through the Schottky into the 330 µF output capacitor. The divider of 47 kΩ over 2.2 kΩ sets 1.25 × (1 + 47/2.2) ≈ 28 V. The 0.22 Ω resistor in the supply feed to the inductor limits the peak current, the 180 Ω resistor gives the driver its collector current (saturated drive), and 1500 pF sets the oscillator. A 1.0 µH and 100 µF LC stage cuts the ripple from 400 to 40 mVpp.
notes: The inductor is 38 turns of #22 AWG on a Magnetics Inc. 55117 toroid.

circuits.title: Step-down converter
circuits.description: Bucks 25 V to 5.0 V at 500 mA. Driver and switch collectors join the sense resistor as a Darlington; the switch emitter feeds the 220 µH inductor, and the Schottky to ground carries the inductor current while the switch is off. The 3.6 kΩ over 1.2 kΩ divider sets 1.25 × (1 + 3.6/1.2) = 5.0 V, 0.33 Ω sets the peak current limit (1.1 A into a short) and 470 pF the oscillator. The optional 1.0 µH and 100 µF stage brings the ripple from 120 to 40 mVpp.
notes: The inductor is 48 turns of #22 AWG on a Magnetics Inc. 55117 toroid.

circuits.title: Voltage inverting converter
circuits.description: Makes -12 V at 100 mA from 4.5 V to 6.0 V. The Darlington switch connects the 88 µH inductor, returned to ground, across the supply; when it opens the inductor pulls its top end below ground and charges the 1000 µF output capacitor negative through the Schottky. The IC ground pin, the timing capacitor and the low end of the divider all sit on the -12 V rail, so the comparator sees the 953 Ω leg of a divider whose 8.2 kΩ leg goes to system ground: |Vout| = 1.25 × (1 + 8.2/0.953) ≈ 12 V. The 0.24 Ω resistor limits the peak current (910 mA into a short) and 1500 pF sets the oscillator. The optional LC stage takes the ripple from 500 to 70 mVpp.
notes: The inductor is 28 turns of #22 AWG on a Magnetics Inc. 55117 toroid.
CO and CF have their positive terminals on ground.

equations.name: Peak switch current, step-up and inverting

operation.text: Runs from 3.0 V to 40 V input with low standby current. The output switch handles up to 1.5 A, the oscillator runs up to 100 kHz, the reference is held to 2 % and the output voltage is set by a divider. Current limiting is built in. Pb-free packages are offered.

Inside are a temperature-compensated 1.25 V reference, a comparator, an oscillator whose duty cycle is gated by active current limiting, a gate and latch, a driver transistor Q2 and the output switch Q1, 79 active transistors in all. Three configurations are covered: step-down, step-up and voltage inverting, each with few external parts.

CT is charged by about 35 µA and discharged by about 220 µA, a ratio near 6.5. With CT = 1.0 nF the frequency is 33 kHz typical (24 to 42 kHz), and the capacitor voltage ramps between about 0.43 V and 1.26 V. Larger CT gives a lower frequency and longer on and off times.

The peak current is sensed across Rsc between VCC and pin 7. At 300 mV typical (250 to 350 mV) across it, the limit acts; Rsc = 0.3 / Ipk(switch). The sense voltage falls with temperature, from about 309 mV at -55 °C to about 248 mV at 125 °C.

With the driver collector (pin 8) tied to the switch collector (pin 1), Q2 and Q1 form a Darlington: it never saturates and drops 1.0 V typical at 1.0 A. With pin 8 fed through its own resistor (82 Ω to VCC in the test) the switch saturates, dropping 0.45 V at 1.0 A with forced β about 20. A saturated switch at low current and high drive can take up to 2.0 µs to turn off, shortening the off time at 30 kHz and above, more so when hot; the recommended forced β = IC(output) / (IC(driver) - 7.0 mA) is 10 or more.

Above 1.5 A of peak current an external transistor takes the switch current. As an NPN its base is driven from the switch emitter (pin 2), with a resistor from pin 2 to ground, in the step-up, step-down and inverting converters alike. For saturated drive the step-up converter feeds pin 1 from the inductor through a resistor R, which can be zero when the input voltage is constant; the step-down and inverting converters use a PNP with its emitter on the sense-resistor side, its base pulled down through a resistor to pin 1 and held off by a resistor to its emitter, with pin 2 grounded.

The CO formula is a starting value: ESR and board layout push the needed capacitance higher. Output ripple adds directly to the line and load regulation error, so a low ripple target is chosen. A 1.0 µH and 100 µF filter after CO lowers the ripple from 400 to 40 mVpp in the step-up converter, from 120 to 40 mVpp in the step-down converter and from 500 to 70 mVpp in the inverting converter.

A design starts from the nominal input Vin, the wanted output Vout and output current Iout, the lowest switching frequency fmin at the chosen Vin and IO, and the wanted peak-to-peak ripple Vripple(pp). Vsat is the switch saturation voltage and VF the rectifier forward drop.
In the markings x is 3 or 4 (33063 or 34063), A is the assembly location, L or WL the wafer lot, Y or YY the year, W or WW the work week and G a Pb-free package.
